detail.readme:
infinidysk

Your media library, streamed from Usenet.

Docs · Quick start · Upgrade from 1.x · Discord · Issues

infinidysk is a Usenet-backed virtual filesystem. Sonarr, Radarr and other Arr apps add it as a SABnzbd download client. It never downloads the release: your media server reads the files over a native FUSE mount or WebDAV, and infinidysk streams them from your Usenet providers on demand. This is infinidysk **2.0**, rewritten in Rust and now in **beta**. On 1.x? See [Looking for 1.x?](#looking-for-1x) > [!WARNING] > **Moving from 1.x to 2.x is a breaking change.** Changing the image name alone is not an upgrade. Follow [Upgrade from 1.x](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/upgrade/), and check [what is not in 2.x yet](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/whats-new/#feature-comparison). ## Why infinidysk - **No download.** The library streams straight from your Usenet providers, so it takes no disk space. - **One container.** A single Rust binary with a built-in FUSE mount. There is no rclone sidecar. - **Drop-in SABnzbd replacement.** Arr apps add it as a SABnzbd download client. No plugin is needed. - **Files stay playable.** Health checks and PAR2 repair find and fix damaged files over time. - **Playback first.** Throughput and prefetch have priority over memory usage. - **Problems you can fix from the UI.** A failure shows one clear reason and a next step, and a read trace shows where playback stalled. ## Quick start A new install. Coming from 1.x? Follow [Upgrade from 1.x](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/upgrade/) instead, so your library and history carry over. ```yaml services: infinidysk: image: ghcr.io/infinidysk/infinidysk-next:edge container_name: infinidysk restart: unless-stopped environment: PUID: 1000 PGID: 1000 TZ: Etc/UTC # your time zone, e.g. Europe/Oslo; the maintenance window follows it ports: - "3000:3000" volumes: - ./config:/config - /mnt:/mnt:rshared - /sys/devices/virtual/bdi:/sys/devices/virtual/bdi:rw devices: - /dev/fuse:/dev/fuse cap_add: - SYS_ADMIN security_opt: - apparmor:unconfined ``` Open `http://:3000`, create the admin account, then add your providers. Do this before exposing the port to an untrusted network: until an admin exists, anyone who reaches the page can create one. | | | |---|---| | **Port** | `3000`, shared by the UI, the SABnzbd API and WebDAV | | **Mount** | The library is mounted at `/mnt/infinidysk` | | **Image** | `ghcr.io/infinidysk/infinidysk-next`, for Linux x64 and arm64 | | **Tags** | `edge` is the newest 2.x release. Every release also has its own `v2.x.y` tag. There is no `latest` tag until 2.0 ships. | Next steps in the docs: 1. [Run with Docker](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/install/docker/) 2. [Providers](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/install/providers/) 3. [Connect your Arr apps](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/install/connect-arr/) 4. [Settings](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/reference/settings/) ## Status 2.0 is in beta. It is a from-scratch rewrite, so it does not have every 1.x feature yet. **In 2.x now** - Streaming over the FUSE mount and WebDAV - SABnzbd API for Arr apps, with symlink import - NZBs with plain files, multipart files and stored RAR4, RAR5 and 7z members - PAR2 verify and repair, health checks and scheduled repair - SQLite and PostgreSQL - Accounts and sign-in - A one-time import of your 1.x config, library and history **Not in 2.x yet** Some 1.x features are still missing. The [feature comparison](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/whats-new/#feature-comparison) lists them. Compressed archives cannot be streamed. infinidysk detects them and fails the import with a clear reason. ## Reporting problems See [Reporting a bug](https://www.infinidysk.com/v2/help/reporting/): the image tag, a support pack from the System page, and for playback problems a read trace. Never post provider passwords or API keys. Release names are not needed; describe the file instead (for example "stored RAR5 episode"). ## Development 1.x bug fixes go to the `v1` branch; everything else targets `main`. Read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for the project rules and [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) before changing the UI. Requires [rustup](https://rustup.rs); the toolchain is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`. ```sh cargo fmt --all --check cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings cargo test --workspace --locked ``` The workspace is a set of crates under [`crates/`](crates/). The product binary is [`crates/infinidysk`](crates/infinidysk); it embeds the web UI from `ui/dist`. The other crates are libraries (NNTP, yEnc, streaming, archives, PAR2, queue, health, VFS, FUSE, WebDAV, database), and dependencies point downward only. To work on the UI, run the backend and the Vite dev server side by side. Vite proxies API calls to `http://127.0.0.1:3000`; set `BACKEND_URL` to point it elsewhere. ```sh INFINIDYSK_CONFIG_DIR="$PWD/scrap/config" cargo run -p infinidysk cd ui && npm ci && npm run dev ``` ## Looking for 1.x? 1.x (the C# version) lives on the [`v1`](https://github.com/infinidysk/infinidysk/tree/v1) branch and keeps the `ghcr.io/infinidysk/infinidysk` image. It gets bug fixes only. Its docs are at [infinidysk.com/v1](https://www.infinidysk.com/v1/).
My fork tracks 1.x. How do I move it to v1? ```sh git fetch upstream git push origin upstream/v1:refs/heads/v1 ``` Then set your fork's default branch to `v1` and sync that branch from now on. A fork with its own commits merges `upstream/v1` instead of `upstream/main`; it is the same history, so there are no new conflicts.
